title: A short database hiccup turns the owner's 'payments off' switches back on
what: When the owner has switched off taking payments in the member app or on the join page, and reading that setting fails for any reason, the server quietly treats both switches as ON and logs nothing. Members and join-page visitors can then be offered online payment the owner said no to. Saving one switch during such a hiccup can also write the other one back to ON.
expected: When the setting cannot be read, payments stay off (or the request fails) and a log line says why; saving one switch never changes the other.
how_often: rare, only when the small database errors
fix_line: When the switches cannot be read, treat them as off and log it; save only the switch that changed

title: Two payment failures are dropped without a single log line
what: When an owner changes payment company keys and the old keys cannot be opened, the old open payment links silently lose the keys used to check them, so money paid on them is no longer picked up automatically. Separately, a correctly signed payment notice that cannot be read is answered 'OK' and thrown away, so the company never resends it. Neither leaves any log line, so nobody can find out why a paid member still shows as owing.
expected: Both cases write a log line naming the gym and provider, so a missed payment can be traced.
fix_line: Add a warning log line in both places

title: The plan 'Pay online' step and the invite page fail with nothing logged, and the pay step has no test
what: When the owner taps 'Pay online' for a MettleUp plan and the HQ server cannot be reached or answers oddly, the owner is told it is unreachable but nothing is logged. The invite and check-in link pages also fall back to a plain page with no log when the gym server does not answer. The plan pay step is the one file here that no test ever runs.
expected: Every failure a person sees leaves a log line, and the plan pay step has a test for its success and failure answers.
who: owners and people opening invite links
how_often: whenever HQ or the gym server is down
fix_line: Log each of these failures and add a small test for the plan pay step

title: The 'who is this sign-in' check is written twice with different rules
what: The AI features and the payment features each have their own copy of the check that asks the gym server who a sign-in belongs to. The AI copy gives up after 8 seconds and refuses demo gyms; the payment copy has no time limit and no demo-gym rule. A fix made in one copy will be missed in the other, and payment screens can hang when the gym server is slow.
expected: One shared sign-in check with one time limit and one set of rules.
how_often: whenever the gym server is slow
fix_line: Make the payment code use the same sign-in check as the AI code

title: 'A day' means three different things in the server's daily limits
what: AI limits reset at midnight India time. The per-address limits on feedback, demo requests and friend enquiries reset at 05:30 India time, because the address is scrambled with the world-clock date. Their overall totals use a rolling 24 hours. A person told 'try again tomorrow' may still be refused next morning, and someone can send double near 05:30. The India-day sum is also copied in four files.
expected: One shared rule for what a day is, used by every limit, matching what the message says.
fix_line: Use one India-day helper for every daily limit

title: About 50 code paths still handle database changes that were applied long ago
what: Across this server about 50 branches handle the case 'this database change is not applied yet', for changes numbered 0006 to 0016. Most are surely live now, so these branches are dead weight, and when a real error happens they log a misleading 'migration not applied?' message. A test also still skips itself 'on Node 20 in CI', but CI has run Node 22 for a month and 19 test files need Node 22 anyway.
expected: Once a database change is live, its fallback branch is removed and errors are logged as errors.
fix_line: Confirm which changes are live, then remove their fallback branches

title: One AI limit test reads the real clock and can fail once around midnight India time
what: The test that checks all gyms together are capped works out today's India date from the real clock, then the server works it out again a moment later. If the run crosses midnight India time between the two, the test fails for no real reason.
expected: The test passes a fixed time to both steps, like the tests around it.
fix_line: Pass a fixed time to the server in that test
